Not oru: oru is for folding paper (origami) or breaking things; clothes and laundry are tatamu.
Not butsukaru: a crashing app ochiru (falls); a frozen one katamaru.
Not ofuro ga dekiru: a bath that is ready waku (heats up). The bath panel announces ofuro ga wakimashita.

english: get dark circles under one's eyes
trap: Dark circles are a noun, kuma, and they dekiru (form), like nikibi ga dekiru.

english: a cockroach shows up, there's a cockroach
trap: Not gokiburi ga iru for one that has just appeared: pests (and ghosts) deru. The usual cry is gokiburi deta!
English 'get food poisoning' gives no verb; Japanese is 'hit by' the food: kaki ni atatta.
Not kinniku o tsukuru: muscle tsuku (attaches); building it on purpose is kinniku o tsukeru.
Not infuru o hiku (hiku goes with kaze only): named illnesses take ni kakaru (infuru ni kakatta, korona ni kakatta).
Not shigoto ga hima ni naru or shizuka ni naru: a busy stretch 'settles' (ochitsuku), the same verb as calming yourself down.
English 'swamped' or 'snowed under' gives no verb: Japanese says you're 'chased by work' (owareru, the passive of ou).

english: turn out fine, clear up (the weather)
trap: Not 'become weather': here tenki alone means fine weather (ashita tenki ni naru kana = hope it's nice tomorrow).
Not ireru or tsunagu: plugs go in with sasu and come out with konsento o nuku. Konsento is the wall socket, not 'consent'.
There's no fog word: glasses 'cloud over' with the same verb as the sky (kumoru).
English 'it says read' has no noun: on LINE the read mark 'attaches' (kidoku ga tsuku), and reading without replying is kidoku suruu.

english: air out a room, let fresh air in
trap: English 'air out' has no Japanese match: you 'swap the air' (irekaeru), usually after opening a window.
Not hana ga ochiru: scattering petals (above all sakura) chiru (sakura mou chitchatta).
Not just takai: 'pricey but worth it' is ne ga haru, built from ne (price) and haru (stretch), words a learner won't connect.

english: work a shift, be on the rota
trap: Not shifuto o suru: you 'enter' a shift, shifuto ni hairu (ashita shifuto haitteru).
Not demae o chuumon suru or kau: you 'take' delivery, demae o toru. Younger people also say uubaa tanomu.

english: be a small eater, not eat much
trap: Not taberu no ga sukunai or chiisai: a small eater's eating is 'thin', shoku ga hosoi.
Plugging something in is sasu (insert), and the socket takes ni: konsento ni sasu. Unplugging is nuku.
Not tsukuru for "make a mess". Making a mess is the one verb chirakasu, the transitive partner of chirakaru.
Not omoi. Heavy makeup is koi (thick, dense) and light makeup is usui; meiku ga koi works the same way.
English 'call' pushes to denwa o kakeru; you yobu (summon) an ambulance, as in the shout kyuukyuusha yonde!
English 'not a morning person' has no calque (asa no hito ja nai is wrong). Say asa ga yowai, and asa ga hayai for an early start or an early riser.
Not waruguchi o hanasu. Badmouthing takes iu, like monku o iu and joudan o iu.

english: skin gets rough or irritated, break out
trap: English 'my skin is dry / bad' pushes to hada ga kawaku or warui. Skin that flares up from stress, cold or lack of sleep areru (hada areta).

english: get over a cold (actively), shake off a cold
trap: English 'get well' has no object, but Japanese makes you naosu the cold: hayaku kaze naoshite ne (get well soon).

english: have a wedding, hold the ceremony
trap: English 'have a wedding' pushes to motsu or aru. A ceremony is held with ageru (shiki o ageru). Casual speech also says kekkonshiki yaru.
Not futsukayoi ga aru. You become hungover (futsukayoi ni natta), or simply say futsukayoi da.

english: be treated (to a meal), let someone pay
trap: Not a passive like gochisou sareru: being treated is gochisou ni naru, like osewa ni naru. The person paying says gochisou suru or ogoru.
Not pointo o morau as the default: points build up, so tamaru. Pointo o tameru is collecting them and pointo o tsukau is spending them.

english: music is playing (in a shop, at a party, on the radio)
trap: Not ongaku ga hiku or ongaku ga suru: a song that's on is kakatteru (or nagareteru), the intransitive of ongaku o kakeru.
Not iyahon o kiru: earphones take suru (or tsukeru), like a watch or a mask, as in iyahon shiteta kara kikoenakatta. Taking them out is hazusu.
Not kaze ga mawaru: an illness going around is 'in fashion', hayatteru. Infuru ga hayatteru is just as common.

english: come with a drink (a set includes it)
trap: Not dorinku to kuru: 'comes with' is tsuku (kore, saarada tsuku?). Tsuku 'arrive' is a different verb.
Not mushiba o motsu: cavities, like pimples and bruises, 'come into being', so dekiru.
Not shio o kakeru: salt is shaken on, furu (same sound as ame ga furu). Kakeru is for liquids like shouyu.
Not iiwake o tsukuru: you 'do' an excuse, iiwake (o) suru.
There is no single verb for 'waste': Japanese says muda ni suru ('make it useless'), and 'a waste of time' is jikan no muda.

english: invite someone over (to your place), have people over
trap: Not shoutai suru, which is for formal invitations such as weddings. Having friends over uses yobu, 'call': tomodachi o uchi ni yobu.
English 'my legs are sore' leads to ashi ga itai. Next-day exercise ache is one noun, kinnikutsuu, with ni naru.
Not netchuushou o toru / morau: you 'become' heatstroke, ni naru, usually in the warning netchuushou ni naranai you ni.

english: be wide awake (and can't get to sleep)
trap: Not me ga sameru, which means waking up. Lying in bed wide awake is me ga saeru (koohii nonda kara me ga saete nerarenai).
English 'is it cooked / done?' leads to yaketa? or ryouri sareta. Asking whether meat is cooked through is mou hi tootteru?

english: (a dish) makes you eat more rice; goes great with rice
trap: English has no matching phrase. Praising a dish as moreish with rice is gohan ga susumu, 'the rice moves forward', also sake ga susumu.
Not gohan o ireru / dasu: dishing rice or soup into a bowl is yosou (gohan yosotte kureru?).

english: the flavour has soaked in (simmered food)
trap: Not aji ga hairu: flavour soaking into simmered food is shimiru (kono daikon, aji ga shimite oishii).

english: get caught at a red light
trap: Not shingou de tomaru / matsu alone: getting stopped by lights is hikkakaru, 'get snagged' (shingou zenbu hikkakatta).
Not himo ga hazureru / aku: a knot coming loose is hodokeru (himo hodoketeru yo). Tying it is himo o musubu.

english: be offended, take it the wrong way
trap: Not okoru or kizutsuku: 'don't take this the wrong way / no offence' is ki o waruku shinaide (ne).

english: look up (a word) in the dictionary
trap: Not jisho o miru / sagasu: consulting a dictionary is hiku, 'pull' (jisho de hiite mita).
'Go home' is kaeru, not iku.
'Speak Japanese' takes o; 'say it in Japanese' takes de.
English 'go back' pushes toward modoru (return); moving backward where you stand is ushiro ni sagaru.
English 'it doesn't work' tempts hataraku or ugokanai; for remedies and methods Japanese says kouka ga nai (or kikanai).
'Keep secrets' is kakushigoto o suru, not motsu.
Purpose takes ni, not o
'Sounds familiar' has no verb for sound; say kikioboe ga aru.
Reading characters or handwriting uses ji, not kotoba.
夜 is read yo here; dawn is 'the night opens'.
omote ni dero is 'step outside (to fight)'; plain 'outside' is usually soto.
English uses a verb (trigger, start); Japanese says X becomes the kikkake.
English 'I was thinking' leads to kangaete ita; for being absorbed in your thoughts people say kangaegoto shiteta.
Being struck is ni + passive utareru; lightning striking a place is kaminari ga ochiru.
Play is not asobu or hiku; roles are enjiru (casually yaku o yaru).

english: find what you were looking for
trap: Find pulls toward mitsukeru; here the thing is the subject of intransitive mitsukaru.
Moving things from place to place is hakobu; motsu only means holding.
English 'make' leads to tsukuru; judgments are handed down with kudasu.
Clothes come off with nugu; toru is for hats and glasses.
'Have' a meal is not motsu; it is toru or taberu.
The path you go down takes o, not kara.
Lay is umu (give birth), not oku (put down).
Damage is received with ukeru, not kurushimu (suffer pain).
Take is noru with ni, not toru.
Win takes ni (win against), not o.
Decisions are handed down with kudasu; everyday speech just says kimeru.
Having a license is motte iru, not aru.
The usual verb is osaeru (press down), not a word for 'control'.
Debt simply exists (aru); there's no verb for 'be in'.
Play a game is suru, not asobu.
'It works' is kiku or kikime ga aru, not ugoku.
Means a café break, coffee included, not just drinking tea.
'Volunteer' as a verb is borantia o suru.
Unplug is nuku (pull out); konsento o nuku is just as common.

english: hear what you have to say
trap: Humble 'hear' is ukagau, not kiku.
Change clothes is kigaeru; fuku o kaeru sounds odd.
About healthy colour, not good looks; kaoiro ga warui = look pale.
A season is crossed with kosu, not survived with ikinokoru.
Read tachi here; shitsu ga warui means poor quality.
Literal only; it doesn't mean holding back words.
English verb 'crack' becomes hibi ga hairu (a crack enters).
Complain is fuman or monku o iu; kureemu is a formal complaint.
Often just fuan desu; anxiety is felt as a noun, not an adjective.
